description:
The biggest single gap: fz has no String module. Utf8 (4 fns) is the entire text surface.

Ship class A + B + D (~27 of 34 core functions) plus Elixir's two SMALL self-owned
tables, and put UAX #29 grapheme breaking behind one seam.

  A -- pure byte work (12): starts_with?/2 ends_with?/2 byte_slice/3 replace_prefix/3
       replace_suffix/3 replace_leading/3 replace_trailing/3 trim/2 trim_leading/2
       trim_trailing/2 upcase/2 downcase/2 (:ascii)
  B -- codepoint decode, no tables (6): codepoints/1 next_codepoint/1 valid?/2
       printable?/2 replace_invalid/2 chunk/2
  D -- thin primitive wrappers (9): contains?/2 count/2 split/3 splitter/3 replace/4
       duplicate/2 to_atom/1 to_integer/1,2 to_float/1

ONE primitive unlocks five: multi-pattern binary search (:binary.match/matches/split/
compile_pattern) gives split/3 + splitter/3 + replace/4 + contains?/2 + count/2.

Elixir generates code from Unicode data for exactly TWO things -- case mapping (2,989
codepoints + 103 special casings) and whitespace (25 codepoints, under 100 clauses).
Everything grapheme- and normalization-shaped is delegated to OTP's :unicode_util,
which is ~1MB compiled and grows ~15% per OTP major (825KB @ OTP27 -> 1.03MB @ 28 ->
1.18MB @ 29). Define next_grapheme_size/1 as the single seam, alias it to
next_codepoint/1 initially, and keep the tables in their OWN module so demand-driven
per-module loading actually pays.

DESIGN GOAL to state explicitly: fz owns both halves, so it can guarantee ONE coherent
Unicode version. Elixir cannot -- in a running system its case mapping is Unicode 17
while OTP's grapheme breaking is Unicode 16.

fz is ahead of Elixir on one axis: String.t/codepoint/grapheme are all literally
'binary' in Elixir (pure documentation), while fz already brands binaries
(Utf8.from_bytes!, fz_brand_bitstring_as_utf8). A real String.t brand gives static
guarantees Elixir cannot, and lets fz DELETE the invalid-byte fallback clauses that
clutter Elixir's codepoints/1, valid?/2 and normalize/2.

Blocked on fz-5xp.1 (idiomatic String is multi-clause binary matching) and fz-5xp.3.
title: String core, staged behind a grapheme seam
